By present order I will decide the question of framing of charge against the accused Praveen Singh (husband of deceased), Pradeep Kumar and Pankaj Kumar Singh (brother- in-law of deceased),
Devanti Devi (mother-in-law of deceased) and Binti Singh (sister-in-law of deceased) in case titled as "State Vs. Praveen Singh & Ors" FIR No. 422/21, PS Chhawla.
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 25.08.2021 vide DD No. 30A information in respect of unfortunate death (suicide) of Alka singh was received.
Post -mortem on the dead body was done by Dr. Pravindra Singh.
On 01.09.2021, Suryavansh Singh father of deceased gave his statement.

5. It is submitted on behalf of prosecution that deceased committed suicide at her matrimonial home because of mental and physical torture.
It is stated that "abetment" differs from one person to another and it is not defined anywhere but intention.

It is stated that it is in the statements of prosecution witnesses who are father, mother and brother of deceased that deceased was mentally and physically treated in such a manner by accused persons that nobody could have come out of such a situation and hence, there is overwhelming evidence on record for framing charge against all accused persons.

has been filed on behalf of the accused persons wherein it is stated that deceased along with the accused persons were residing happily and peacefully.
It is contended on behalf of accused persons that there is no evidence on record to indicate that accused persons instigated deceased to commit suicide.
It is submitted that the deceased remained with the accused persons for almost 9  years and during this period neither deceased nor her family made any complaint against accused persons.

It is further submitted that though the prosecution has relied upon the audio clip in which some heated exchanges took place but that audio clip is about 14 months prior to the death of deceased and that too does not indicate that deceased was forced to commit suicide.

Thus, it is case of a suicidal death.
9. To attract an offence punishable U/s 306 IPC it must be proved that a person charged for the offence has an mens-rea to commit the offence.

It also requires an active act or direct act which led the deceased to commit suicide seeing no option and this act must have been intended to push the deceased into such a position that he/she committed suicide.

entities.text: Geo Varghese v. State of Rajasthan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In our country, while suicide in itself is not an offence as a person committing suicide goes beyond the reach of law but an attempt to suicide is considered to be an offence under Section 309 IPC.
The abetment of suicide by anybody is also an offence under Section 306 IPC.

It would be relevant to set out Section 306 of the IPC which reads as under:
"306. Abetment of suicide.

--If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine."
14. Though, the IPC does not define the word 'Suicide' but the ordinary dictionary meaning of suicide is 'self-killing'.

The word is derived from a modern latin word 'suicidium', 'sui' means SC No.
551/2022 State Vs. Praveen Singh & Ors 'oneself' and 'cidium' means 'killing'.

sentences.text: Thus, the word suicide implies an act of 'self-killing'.
In other words, act of death must be committed by the deceased himself, irrespective of the means adopted by him in achieving the object of killing himself.

15. Section 306 of IPC makes abetment of suicide a criminal offence and prescribes punishment for the same.
16.
The ordinary dictionary meaning of the word 'instigate' is to bring about or initiate, incite someone to do something.

This Court in the case of Ramesh Kumar v. State of Chhattisgarh has defined the word 'instigate' as under:
"Instigation is to goad, urge forward, provoke, incite or encourage to do an act."
17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

In the case of S.S. Cheena v. Vijay Kumar Mahajan, it was observed as under:
"Abetment involves a mental process of instigating a person or intentionally aiding a person in doing of a thing.

sentences.text: The intention of the legislature and the ratio of the cases decided by the Supreme Court is clear that in order to convict a person under Section 306 IPC there has to be a clear mens rea to commit the offence.

It also requires an active act or direct act which led the deceased to commit suicide seeing no option and that act must have been intended to push the deceased into such a position that he committed suicide."

29. The ingredients of Section 306 IPC have been extensively laid out in M. Arjunan v.State, SC No.
551/2022 State Vs. Praveen Singh & Ors represented by its Inspector of Police

which are as under:
"The essential ingredients of the offence under Section 306 I.P.C. are : (i) the abetment; (ii) the intention of the accused to aid or instigate or abet the deceased to commit suicide.
The act of the accused, however, insulting the deceased by using abusive language will not, by itself, constitute the abetment of suicide.
There should be evidence capable of suggesting that the accused intended by such act to instigate the deceased to commit suicide.

Unless the ingredients of instigation/abetment to commit suicide are satisfied, accused cannot be convicted under Section 306 I.P.C."
17.

As stated in above authoritative judgment, to constitute an offence U/s 306 IPC there must not only the mens rea but also a direct evidence to establish that there was an active act by the accused which led the deceased to commit suicide.

In present case, there might be some differences between deceased and her husband or for that matter she was maltreated by her in-laws but there is no material on record which indicates either mens rea or any evidence of any active role of accused persons for driving deceased to commit suicide.
Rather in their statements sons of deceased have pointed out towards normal relations between deceased and her in-laws.

In the case of Sajjan Kumar vs. CBI (2010) 9 SCC 368, Hon'ble Apex Court on consideration of the various decisions about the scope of Sections 227 and 228 of the Code, laid down the following principles:
(i) The Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under Section 227 of the Cr.P.C. has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.
The test to determine prima facie case would depend upon the facts of each case.

ii) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained, the Court will be fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.

iii) The Court cannot act merely as a Post Office or a mouthpiece of the prosecution but has to consider the broad probabilities of the case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court, any basic infirmities, etc.

However, at Sc No. 551/2022 State vs . Praveen Singh & Ors on 8 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55604274/
5 this stage, there cannot be a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial.
iv) If on the basis of the material on record, the Court could form an opinion that the accused might have committed offence, it can frame the charge, though for conviction the conclusion is required to be proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused has committed the offence.
v) At the time of framing of the charges, the probative value of the material on record cannot be gone into but before framing a SC No. 551/2022 State Vs. Praveen Singh &
Ors charge the Court must apply its judicial mind on the material placed on record and must be satisfied that the commission of offence by the accused was possible.

sentences.text: vi) At the stage of Sections227 and 228, the Court is required to evaluate the material and documents on record with a view to find out if the facts emerging therefrom taken at their face value discloses the existence of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offence.

For this limited purpose, sift the evidence as it cannot be expected even at that initial stage to accept all that the prosecution states as gospel truth even if it is opposed to common sense or the broad probabilities of the case.

vii) If two views are possible and one of them gives rise to suspicion only, as distinguished from grave suspicion, the trial Judge will be empowered to discharge the accused and at this stage, he is not to see whether the trial will end in conviction or acquittal.
19.

It is evident that there is no material on record which gives rise to grave suspicion against accused persons to have committed the offence of abetment of suicide nor there is any allegation in respect of specific demand of dowry or cruelty inflicted on deceased by accused persons on account of demand of dowry so to frame charge under Section 498A IPC,
20.

Considering the principles as laid down in above stated authoritative pronouncements, it has to be concluded that SC No. 551/2022 State Vs. Praveen Singh & Ors charge for the offence punishable under Section 306/498-A/34 IPC is not made out against accused persons.
